 A Texas lawmaker is pushing legislation that would require stronger security tech on the cards families use to access SNAP benefits after millions of dollars were stolen from households across the state. State Senator Judith Zaffirini, a Laredo Democrat, filed Senate Bill 374 last week. If passed, the bill would require electronic benefit transfer cards used for SNAP and the state's financial assistance program to contain security chips capable of processing transactions when inserted into a card reader. This legislation is arriving after an investigation by KVUE found that more than $21 million in SNAP benefits had been stolen from Texas families, and nearly 40,000 Texas households reported stolen benefits since May 2023. Why It Matters SNAP provides food assistance to low-income households, but the cards used to distribute those benefits have become targets for criminals using skimming and cloning techniques. With skimming, criminals can merely place devices on payment terminals that capture information stored on a card's magnetic stripe. The stolen card data can then be used to create fraudulent cards and drain a recipient's account, sometimes shortly after the monthly benefits are deposited. Restoring the stolen benefits can also be exceedingly difficult. In Texas, more than $6.7 million in reimbursement claims filed in 2025 went unpaid, according to the KVUE investigation. What Is Senate Bill 374? Senate Bill 374 would require the Texas Health and Human Services Commission to ensure EBT cards issued for SNAP and the state's financial assistance program contain an integrated electronic chip. Under the legislation's proposed timeline, Texas would have to begin issuing chip-equipped EBT cards on September 1, 2028. By March 1, 2029, every EBT card used to access the affected benefits would have to comply with the new requirement. If a federal waiver or authorization is needed first, the bill allows implementation of the relevant provision to be delayed until federal approval is obtained. Judith Zaffirini told KVUE that SNAP recipients deserve protections against electronic theft comparable to those available to consumers using conventional payment cards. "SNAP recipients should have the same protections against electronic theft that consumers have come to expect from their credit and debit cards," Zaffirini said. The cost of moving Texas' EBT system to chip cards has not yet been determined, but the bill could reduce or outright prevent future theft. “I believe the bill could have an immediate impact, particularly in reducing card skimming,” Kevin Thompson, the CEO of 9i Capital Group, told Newsweek. “However, the reality is that by the time legislation is passed and implemented, fraudsters may have already moved on to another method. We could effectively be passing legislation just to catch up with a problem that continues to evolve.” How Many Households Have Reported Stolen Benefits? Nearly 40,000 Texas households have reported stolen benefits since May 2023, according to state data. KVUE’s investigation found that more than $21 million in SNAP benefits had been stolen from Texas families. However, the problem is not unique to Texas. Congress has authorized federal replacement of SNAP benefits stolen through card skimming and cloning for this very reason, and the USDA Food and Nutrition Service approved replacement plans submitted by all 50 states, Washington, D.C., Guam and the U.S. Virgin Islands under that temporary authority. “The most worrying aspect of this fraud is that many victims have done absolutely nothing wrong, as criminals use card-skimming devices, stolen PINs, and fraudulent transactions to drain accounts, sometimes immediately after benefits are deposited,” Alex Beene, a financial literacy instructor for the University of Tennessee at Martin, told Newsweek. “Legislation like this could make a substantial difference, as modern security chips would make it significantly harder for criminals to duplicate benefit cards.” Which States Use EBT Cards for SNAP? All 50 states use electronic benefit transfer systems to issue SNAP benefits. SNAP benefits are loaded electronically onto an EBT account and participants use their state's corresponding EBT card to purchase eligible food. But while EBT is the nationwide way that SNAP benefits are delivered, the Texas Lone Star Card is Texas' unique version of an EBT card. What Happens Next Senate Bill 374 was filed ahead of the 2027 Texas Legislature session, which begins January 12. For the requirements to become law, the proposal would have to clear both chambers of the Legislature and receive the governor's approval. “Although this sounds like a solution, the real question is what types of fraud chip-enabled cards would actually prevent. Is this truly the right answer, or are we simply chasing our tails and destined to remain one step behind?” Thompson said.
